items.name: Lab
items.what: Each lane has a pretend account in the lab, and 20 random twins that buy random stocks on the same days. A lane shows skill only if it beats its own twins.
items.runs: Weekdays at 22:15 Central time, with a second try at 22:45.
items.can_show: No word before 20 days. A lane reads “clearly ahead” only after 60 days and 20 closed trades, with a lead of 2.5 standard deviations over its twins.

recorded.label: Closed trades of the lab accounts
Lanes that trade in the paper account

due.what: First chance of a clear result
due.rule: At 60 recorded days, if a lane also has 20 closed trades.

items.name: News reader shadow
items.what: Each night an AI model (Claude Opus) reads the news of 20 flagged stocks in three setups: the real news, no news, and another stock's news. The real setup's orders go to the News reader lane. The other two setups are a check and never trade.
items.runs: Weekdays at 19:20 Central time. The score step runs at 19:50.
items.can_show: No result before about 60 nights. Then the real-news setup must beat the other two setups to show that the news helps.

recorded.label: Stocks flagged on the last night
Stocks read on the last night
Readings on the last night, all setups

items.name: Volatility shadow
items.what: Each night it records our volatility forecast and the 30-day implied volatility from option prices for 40 stocks. Later it compares both with the volatility that came. It reports only and never trades.
items.can_show: No effect number before the counted score. The score runs once, after 60 counted days and 21 more trading days for the result.

recorded.label: Stocks recorded on the last night
Results that came in so far

due.rule: Once, after 60 counted days and 21 more trading days.

items.name: Option price recorder
items.what: It records the day's option prices for every stock in the universe. It keeps data only and never trades. With these prices we can test an option lane later.
items.runs: Weekdays at 15:05 Central time, with a second try at 16:05.
items.can_show: Nothing on its own. It builds a price history, because the system had no past option prices.
